描述_EN: from surviving mamluk textiles, it seems that blue was a favoured colour. similar textiles have not been found in china and it is possible that these silks were made specially for the mamluk empire (1250-1517). mamluk and other textiles from the islamic world are known to incorporate scripts into their designs, so the inclusion of a longevity ideograph may have been a deliberate move. this fragment is part of a group of chinese silks in the v&a collection , broadly dated between the late thirteenth century and the mid-fifteenth century, and supposedly came from the medieval urban centre of fustat in egypt. the pattern of this silk in pale blue and silvery beige consists of a circular medallion with the stylized chinese character shou, meaning 'longevity', and motif of a flaming jewel that fills the spaces in between these medallions. this fragment is part of a group of chinese silks in the v&a collection, broadly dated between the late thirteenth century and the mid-fifteenth century, and supposedly came from the medieval urban centre of fustat in egypt. the weaving may have been carried out in china and the silks then exported westwards, or it could have been done outside china by islamic craftsmen familiar with chinese patterning.
描述_ZN: 从现存的马穆鲁克纺织品来看，蓝色似乎是一种受欢迎的颜色。 类似的纺织品在中国没有发现，这些丝绸有可能是专门为马穆鲁克帝国（1250-1517）制作的。 马穆鲁克和其他来自伊斯兰世界的纺织品都知道将文字纳入他们的设计中，所以加入一个长寿的表意文字可能是一个有意的举动。 这个片段是V&A收藏的一组中国丝绸的一部分，时间大致在13世纪晚期和15世纪中期，据说来自埃及的中世纪城市中心Fustat。 这块淡蓝色和银色米色的丝绸的图案由一个圆形的徽章组成，徽章上有 "寿 "字，意为 "长寿"，徽章之间的空间里有一个燃烧的宝石图案。 这块碎片是V&A收藏的一组中国丝绸的一部分，时间大致在13世纪末到15世纪中叶，据说来自埃及的中世纪城市中心福斯塔特。 织造可能是在中国进行的，然后丝绸向西出口，也可能是在中国以外由熟悉中国图案的伊斯兰工匠完成。
